title: Coding agents discover routing with conditional progress guarantees
summary: Human-directed coding agents synthesized Core-Graph-Anchored Routing, combining recoverable motion commitments with throughput heuristics. Eight paired simulated runs on a calibrated warehouse layout showed 58.9% higher throughput than the proprietary baseline. The source supplies a conditional safety and finite-progress proof; no physical fleet deployment is established.
ai_technology: Codex 5.6 Sol and Codex Astra coding agents, with Fable model assistance
organization: KNAPP; Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Columbia University; University of British Columbia

evidence.tested: Six simulated warehouse layouts, eight paired two-hour runs per layout; one calibrated baseline and five uncalibrated baseline comparisons. An additional synthetic layout was evaluated without changing the policy.
evidence.unknown: Human steering and simulation-specific selection limit transfer. The theorem assumes valid core-graph separation/connectivity/vacancies, finite motions, recoverable initialization, service coverage and correctly implemented runtime checks. Some storage nodes require extra vacancies beyond the simplified theorem. We did not reproduce the proof or execution; no deployment claim.
evidence.ai_role: Coding agents proposed, implemented and diagnosed the new routing architecture from objectives and constraints, using simulation feedback. Models operate during discovery, not in the compiled planner.

source_review.scope: Actual v1 formulation, coding-agent Methods, warehouse Results, limitations and Appendix A proof read. Current history lists v1 October 19 and v2 October 20; represented result is already in v1, without an absolute-priority claim.
